caption: Does “when I awake” predict resurrection? It may express hope beyond death—but ordinary waking remains possible, and Luke never connects Jesus with this verse.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 17 predict resurrection? The writer expects to see God’s face and be satisfied “when I awake.” Christians connect that awakening with Jesus rising.
slides.body: The writer expects to see God’s face and be satisfied “when I awake.” Christians connect that awakening with Jesus rising.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 17 predict resurrection?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 17:15: When I awake, I will be satisfied in Your presence.
slides.body: When I awake, I will be satisfied in Your presence.
slides.heading: Ps 17:15

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Lk 24:6, BSB: He is not here; He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee:
slides.body: He is not here; He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee:
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Lk 24:6

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: It may be hope beyond death The contrast with people satisfied only in this life can suggest a greater awakening and final vindication.
slides.body: The contrast with people satisfied only in this life can suggest a greater awakening and final vindication.
slides.heading: It may be hope beyond death

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But “awake” is ambiguous It may mean ordinary sleep or renewed awareness of God. Luke never links Jesus’s resurrection to this verse.
slides.body: It may mean ordinary sleep or renewed awareness of God. Luke never links Jesus’s resurrection to this verse.
slides.heading: But “awake” is ambiguous

title: When I awake
